answer: A haven hall admits one pearl per identity. Each applicant posts a 75-credit bond keyed to its serial and files a lantern-lit assay of diameter, weight, and luster under a lantern spectrum. The haven auditor recomputes weight from the pearl assay table; over 3% mismatch, a reused serial, or a wrong key burns the bond. Fees start at 41; the kth identity from one wallet pays 41+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5036 and 1000 fakes pay 2538500 plus 75000 locked. A rented-pearl ring fails on a reused serial, which burns bonds; an honest applicant pays 41 once and reclaims the bond after audit.
